title: Rational root theorem
sentences: Solutions of the equation are also called roots or zeros of the polynomial on the left side.
The rational root theorem is a special case (for a single linear factor) of Gauss's lemma on the factorization of polynomials.
The integral root theorem is the special case of the rational root theorem when the leading coefficient is an = 1.
The theorem is used to find all rational roots of a polynomial, if any.
It gives a finite number of possible fractions which can be checked to see if they are roots.

If a rational root x = r is found, a linear polynomial (x – r) can be factored out of the polynomial using polynomial long division, resulting in a polynomial of lower degree whose roots are also roots of the original polynomial.
